name: Background gaps
sentence: How often proseg tries background instead of a cell at a cell's edge. Low: cells fill free space sooner. High: they fill it more slowly.
info: Made-up cells, started from cells only: this cell's starting outline misses a bite next to A holding little of its own RNA and some of another neighbour's (not A's). Other settings at proseg's defaults. Each panel: the middle of 27 copies. On real 500 µm squares, 0.01 or 0.1 instead of 0.05 left the pink dots within noise; with 0.3, one real cell's count of its neighbour's RNA fell from 20 to 13 (probable).
statTip: Pink dots in this panel: a neighbour's RNA this cell's count keeps. At 0.3 the cell reaches them more slowly; by the end the counts are about the same here, its own RNA too. In the final settling 0.3 leaves a little more of a neighbour's RNA in gaps, uncounted: too little to see.
